one_liner: Nemotron never answers the patient; it triages the symptom, audits another model's draft advice, and a deterministic Python gate() decides whether the draft is safe to show.
problem: Digital-health companies cannot ship symptom features because nobody can explain to legal/compliance why any individual LLM answer was safe; black-box safety scores give no named reason and no tunable threshold.
target_user: Telehealth / digital-health product and compliance teams (enterprise), medical as the wedge; legal/claims/financial guidance later.
core_loop: Symptom text -> Nemotron router (acuity, red flags, fast/deep path; emergency hard-stops) -> GPT-4o-mini drafts advice -> Nemotron verifier (thinking mode) returns structured findings JSON -> gate() applies 8 ordered rules -> pass/revise/escalate rendered in a Gradio panel with stage trace and rule ladder; verifier dropdown swaps judge or removes it (ablation).
mocked_or_hardcoded: Nothing mocked; eval set (43 cases) is synthetic, built by Nemotron Ultra corrupting 10 hand-written scenarios. Clean controls are hand-written ideal drafts. Disk cache for API calls. README references docs/FINDINGS.md, evidence/policy_curve.png and notebooks/ that are not in the repo; chart counts (26/31) differ slightly from README (27/33) across runs.
demo_risks: Lives in a Colab notebook; demo is a Gradio share URL launched from the last cell. Needs NVIDIA API key and OpenRouter key live; verifier with thinking takes 15-45 s per run; some Nemotron slugs not entitled on the account. Single-sample temperature-0 eval, no clinician review.
ui_experience: Gradio Blocks app with custom dark CSS: symptom textbox, drafter/verifier/schema dropdowns, example inputs, a staged narrative trace (who did what), findings list, and a gate ladder highlighting the rule that fired with lower rules greyed out. Functional, not flashy.
integrity_flags: Solo project, 6 commits all 9/19. Credits Claude for code review, debugging and demo front end. Keys read from Colab secrets, none committed. README slightly overclaims repo artifacts that are absent.
ai_scaffolding_flags: None (no CLAUDE.md/AGENTS.md). Notebook prose is heavy but code is 3.1k lines.
novelty_notes: Judge-model + deterministic policy layer is a known enterprise pattern, but applying it as 'model reports observations, code decides' with a schema-gap diagnosis (v1 could not see omissions) and a recall-vs-coverage comparison is uncommon at a hackathon.
need_notes: Well-argued procurement/compliance pain, but no customer quotes or data; medical framing is a hypothesis.
wow_moment: Set the verifier dropdown to None and watch raw unchecked advice ship; then the table showing GPT-4o-mini blocks 8/10 safe answers because it rates how sick the patient is, not how unsafe the answer is.
score_rationale: Nails the Nemotron track brief: non-chat role, ablation, cross-model comparison, documented failures with a real eval set. Core loop runs live against real APIs but only inside a Colab/Gradio notebook with slow verifier calls, and the UI is a plain Gradio panel. Need is plausible enterprise pain without evidence.
judge_summary: A solo Nemotron-track entry where Nemotron is the auditor, not the chatbot: it triages a symptom, checks another model's draft, and Python rules decide. Comes with a 43-case eval, a coverage-vs-recall argument, and a live ablation toggle. Gradio demo, no product polish.

one_liner: An ElevenLabs voice agent ('June') that older adults call or get called by to hear safe-to-spend, bills and unusual charges, gated by a spoken PIN, while a family caretaker supervises budgets, approvals and fraud alerts on a web dashboard.
problem: Adult children who moved out cannot see or help with an aging parent's money; seniors will not use apps, and elder fraud (gift cards, wires) goes unnoticed until it is too late.
target_user: Family caretakers of older adults (dashboard) and the older adult member (phone only, no app).
best_fit_tracks: MLH bonus tracks: Best Use of Gemini API
core_loop: Inbound call -> /api/elevenlabs/init matches caller ID to a member and starts a call session -> agent asks PIN -> /api/elevenlabs/tools/$tool webhooks (verify_pin, get_balance, upcoming bills, affordability, propose/confirm change, flag transaction) read/write Postgres with server-side verification gating -> post-call webhook stores transcript; alerts engine evaluates shortfall/unusual/bill/deposit rules and places outbound calls via ElevenLabs; caretaker dashboard shows summary, charts, approvals, notifications; /bank page has demo buttons to inject a transaction and run alerts.
mocked_or_hardcoded: BANK_PROVIDER=mock serves seeded DB rows (Plaid sandbox path also implemented). Demo login shortcuts (maria@demo.dev, 'simulate new user'). Plaid webhook signature not verified (TODO). Vercel cron daily only, so alerts are triggered manually in the demo. Native Expo app is the starter template (Tab One/todos).
demo_risks: The headline moment needs a configured ElevenLabs agent, Twilio number, public tunnel and a phone on stage; any of those failing leaves only the dashboard. Gemini fraud button errors without a key. Three names for the same product (NestEgg, June, 'Call Robin', steward/nester) from late renames; landing README is still the Better-T-Stack template.
ui_experience: About ten routes: landing with a hand-coded procedural SVG mountain/pine hero that parallaxes with the cursor, caretaker dashboard with balance/spending charts, transactions, budgets, approvals, notifications panel, onboarding, accounts, plus a large-type 'senior view' (20px+ text, 64px targets, one Call button). shadcn components, dark mode, skeleton loading states. Polished for a hackathon.
integrity_flags: Started from Better-T-Stack scaffold (README, todos route, native app untouched); all 52 commits fall inside the hackathon window with 4 contributors. No secrets committed (env schemas only). Name inconsistency across screens.
ai_scaffolding_flags: Large .agents/skills and .claude/skills trees (thousands of lines, shipped by the scaffold); docs/plans/voice-line.md is written as milestone tasks 'sized for one coding-agent task' with ADRs; CONTEXT.md glossary. Code (~12k lines TS) still outweighs docs.
novelty_notes: Voice-first, no-app banking for seniors with proactive outbound calls, PIN gating on both directions, permission tiers (instant / notify / needs approval) and a safe-to-spend number is a thoughtful twist on the fintech-for-families category.
need_notes: Elder financial vulnerability is real and specific; design shows domain thinking (quiet hours, dedupe keys, no amounts before PIN) but no user research or data cited.
wow_moment: Caretaker clicks 'inject $400 gift-card charge' on the dashboard, and a phone on the table rings: June greets Dot by name, asks for her PIN, then warns about the charge.
score_rationale: Strong ElevenLabs track fit that stacks with Compound and Gemini. Full voice tool surface, alerts engine, tests and a polished multi-screen dashboard with custom art. Marked down for heavy reliance on live telephony, mock bank data, template leftovers and naming churn.
judge_summary: A voice agent seniors can phone about their money, with a caretaker dashboard that approves changes and injects fraud scenarios live. Big, well-structured build; the demo lands or dies on the phone call actually connecting.

one_liner: A physical-therapy journal: log workouts, routines, schedule, PT plans and pain levels in a vanilla-JS web app backed by a Spring Boot API.
problem: People in rehab need to track prescribed exercises and pain over time; the README does not articulate a specific pain point beyond 'PT journal and progress tracker'.
target_user: Individuals doing physical therapy or recovering from injury.
core_loop: Hash route -> fetch corrective-api.onrender.com/api/* -> Spring controllers -> seeded in-memory DataStore -> render dashboard cards, workout/routine/schedule/plan/pain lists, dialogs to create/delete, SVG pain chart.
mocked_or_hardcoded: All data is in-memory and seeded at boot; no users, no persistence (restart wipes everything, and everyone shares the same data). README admits no profiles yet and that the site is slow. Reference/ folder holds a v0-generated Next.js version that is not deployed.
demo_risks: Render free-tier cold start (frontend even shows 'the API may be waking up'); shared global state; no auth. Low risk otherwise: static frontend, simple CRUD.
ui_experience: Tidy hand-written CSS design system (Plus Jakarta Sans, teal/coral palette, dark mode toggle, sidebar + bottom nav, dialogs, toasts, skeletons, empty/error states) across 6 views with an inline SVG pain-trend chart. Basic but clean.
integrity_flags: README states 'we basically just used AI for everything'; the SPA + API commit is authored by 'v0' (Vercel v0). An entire workout-tracker Next.js app was uploaded then deleted, then re-added under reference/ as the v0 original. First-timer team, all commits within the event.
ai_scaffolding_flags: None (no CLAUDE.md/AGENTS.md); honest disclosure in README.
novelty_notes: Workout/PT tracker is a category judges have seen many times; no distinctive mechanism.
need_notes: Plausible but generic; no evidence, no PT-specific insight beyond pain logging.
wow_moment: None; the pain chart is the closest thing to a moment.
score_rationale: Generic tracker with CRUD working end to end but no persistence or users, generated largely by v0 as the team openly admits. Clean basic UI. Fits only the beginner track.
judge_summary: First-timers' AI-generated PT journal: six CRUD screens on an in-memory Spring Boot API. Works, looks tidy, nothing memorable.

one_liner: Personalized food guidance for people with Crohn's: scores every food against your own meal and symptom history, scans restaurant menus with Gemini, ranks nearby restaurants, and talks you through recipes.
problem: Universal 'safe food' lists fail Crohn's patients because tolerance is individual; people need to learn their own patterns from their own logs.
target_user: People living with Crohn's disease (all ages) who want to understand their relationship with food.
claimed_tracks: MLH bonus tracks: Best Use of Gemini API
best_fit_tracks: MLH bonus tracks: Best Use of Gemini API
core_loop: Seeded 120-day demo profile (or Postgres for signed-in users) -> lib/scoring/compatibility.ts blends exact-food history (14h symptom window), learned trait sensitivities, general traits and phase/restrictions into a 0-100 score with factor breakdown -> pages: search, food detail, log meal/symptom, menu scan (photo or text -> Gemini JSON, keyword-trait fallback -> scored dishes), near-you (hardcoded Oakland restaurants ranked by best dish), cook (guided steps read aloud via /api/voice -> ElevenLabs, browser TTS fallback), progress charts.
mocked_or_hardcoded: 60+ foods, recipes and the restaurant list with illustrative menus are hardcoded; demo user history is seeded. Every integration degrades gracefully: no DB -> in-memory guest store, no Gemini -> local explanations and regex trait inference, no ElevenLabs -> browser speech. Local auth fallback when no DB.
demo_risks: Low: designed to run with zero config. Gemini vision on a live menu photo depends on API/model availability (model id gemini-3.6-flash set in env). ElevenLabs may 402 on the account (handled). Guest data lost on restart.
ui_experience: Warm custom palette (cream/moss/clay, Fraunces + Outfit), stagger/rise animations, score rings and badges, sparkline and Recharts trend charts, chips, cards, empty/loading/error pages, guest banner, account menu, mobile capture=environment file input for menus. Six feature areas plus auth. Polished consumer-health feel.
integrity_flags: An ElevenLabs API key (sk_cad7...) was committed to .env.example in commit 4d6622a and blanked two commits later (still in history). Otherwise clean: 19 commits, 4 contributors, all within the event.
ai_scaffolding_flags: CLAUDE.md product spec (~200 lines, includes target tracks and coding workflow for the agent) plus auto-inserted Next.js agent rules. Code (~9k lines) far outweighs docs.
novelty_notes: IBD food/symptom diaries exist; the twist is a transparent per-user compatibility model applied to menus, nearby restaurants and recipes, always framed as an estimate.
need_notes: Specific patient population with a genuine, often-stated pain ('everyone's triggers are different'); no user quotes or data in repo but the framing shows domain awareness and safety restraint.
wow_moment: Snap a photo of a real restaurant menu and watch the dishes come back ranked against your own logged history, each with a 'why'.
score_rationale: Complete, polished, fault-tolerant product with a real scoring model and three sponsor integrations that each add something. Category is known, so novelty is moderate; Xtract claim is a stretch, Seed Round and Gemini fit well. Leaked key in history is a hygiene ding.
judge_summary: A calm, well-finished Crohn's food companion: personal compatibility scores, Gemini menu scanning, nearby-restaurant picks and spoken cooking steps, all working without any keys. Memorable for the menu photo -> ranked dishes moment.

score_rationale: Empty repository: one README line and no code.
judge_summary: Empty repo, nothing submitted beyond a title.

one_liner: A pixel-art turn-based game where you run a company in the Amazon; your real stress, read from your webcam via Presage SmartSpectra, shortens your turn timer and makes the greedy, forest-destroying cards more likely to appear.
problem: Illustrates how time pressure and stress push decision-makers toward short-term extractive choices; an awareness/education game about deforestation rather than a stated user pain.
target_user: Players / students; anyone curious how their own physiology changes their choices.
stack: Pixel-art PNG assets + custom TTF font
core_loop: Story screen -> 18 turns over 3 acts alternating human and bot company -> drawChoices() picks 3 cards weighted by current stress (calm/mid/high tiers) -> choice applies profit/trust/stress/forest deltas -> tile grid greys out as forest health drops -> random events in later acts -> timeout auto-picks the highest-profit card -> ending reveals winner then 'the real number' (hectares lost, panicked decisions). usePresageSocket receives {stress} from bridge.mjs, which maps pulse and breathing rate to 0-100; simulated stress ramp when no bridge.
mocked_or_hardcoded: Simulated stress fallback runs whenever the bridge is not connected (the label says '(simulated)'). Tile data file is unused; the grid is 120 identical forest tiles. Bot opponent is a heuristic. main.jsx is a leftover diagnostic error-overlay entry point.
demo_risks: Live path needs a SMARTSPECTRA_API_KEY, a webcam with good lighting and the Node bridge running locally; the SDK also needs network to validate the key. If it fails the game still plays with fake stress, which weakens the pitch. README has no description.
ui_experience: Full-screen forest photo backdrop, wooden-frame pixel GUI panels, four pixel-art stat bars (profit, trust, stress, forest), a 12x10 tile grid with random tile art that turns grey as the forest dies, choice cards tinted by risk tier, a turn timer, story/event/ending screens with a two-stage reveal. Charming and playable in three minutes.
integrity_flags: Uses a stock forest PNG and a stock pixel-sky JPG. Vite template README left in place with only team names added. 69 commits from 3 people, all within the event. No secrets.
ai_scaffolding_flags: .agents/skills/using-smartspectra/SKILL.md and skills-lock.json (Presage-provided SDK skill). No CLAUDE.md.
novelty_notes: Biofeedback-driven strategy game is a genuinely new mechanism at this event: physiology is a game input that degrades your option set, not just a displayed number.
need_notes: No user pain; it is an awareness piece. The ending's 'what that actually cost' reveal gives it a point.
wow_moment: Judge sits down, the stress bar flips from 'simulated' to 'live', and as they hurry their pulse shortens the timer and the land-grab card starts showing up every turn.
score_rationale: Real Presage SDK integration feeding a working game loop with a clear mechanic and a message; no LLM anywhere. Rough edges (unused data, debug overlay, empty README) and a weak 'need' story, but it is the kind of thing judges can play and feel.
judge_summary: A pixel-art deforestation game where your webcam-measured stress shrinks the clock and stacks the deck with greedy cards. Playable, themed, and physical; the Presage hookup is real with a simulated fallback.

one_liner: A bank chat assistant (React Native) whose LLM agent can only read the signed-in customer's data through policy-gated tools, issues server-built dispute and fraud-triage forms instead of acting, and hands cases to a staff review dashboard that credits the account in a Firestore transaction.
problem: Disputing a duplicate or unrecognized charge and locking a card is slow and confusing; chatbots that act on money are risky, so the agent should surface and structure, never decide.
target_user: Retail bank customers (chat app) and bank dispute-review staff (dashboard).
stack: pydantic-ai with Anthropic Claude (haiku router, opus agent)
core_loop: Message -> regex rules then a tiny Claude Haiku classifier decide scope -> Claude agent with typed tools (accounts, transactions, duplicates, start_dispute_form, start_fraud_triage, dispute status) reading Firestore for the session's user_id -> chat returns prose plus structured cards (dispute form, triage form, case card, suggestions) -> customer submits form -> POST /disputes creates case (irreversible tier, confirmation required); card lock/replace via triage -> staff dashboard lists pending cases, approve/reject/provisional credit -> balance and reversal written transactionally.
mocked_or_hardcoded: Bank accounts/transactions are synthetic Firestore documents (no seed script in repo). Welcome text promises transfers and bill pay the agent explicitly declines. Server-side keyword lists (DISPUTE_INTENT etc.) backstop the model when it fails to issue a form.
demo_risks: Requires ANTHROPIC_API_KEY with credits (chat route surfaces 'out of credits' hints), a Firebase service-account JSON in backend/, Firestore connectivity and Firebase Auth. Opus latency per turn. No README describing the project, tracks or how to run the three apps.
ui_experience: Chase-styled chat screen (blue palette, app logo, online status, typing indicator, day dividers, grouped bubbles, tool trace, suggestion chips, scroll-to-bottom) with inline dispute/triage form cards; login/signup; a separate staff dashboard with disputes queue, tool policy list and settings. Attractive standard fintech look, no unusual interaction.
integrity_flags: All 28 commits within the event by 3 contributors. Firebase admin key referenced by filename but not committed. Frontend and dashboard READMEs are untouched Expo/Next templates. Uses Anthropic models, no Nemotron.
ai_scaffolding_flags: dashboard/CLAUDE.md (@AGENTS.md) and AGENTS.md are the auto-generated Next.js agent rules only. Extensive design-rationale comments in Python suggest AI-assisted authoring; docs are small relative to code.
novelty_notes: Banking chatbot is a familiar category; the twist is the explicit policy tiers (read / reversible / irreversible + confirmation), server-issued forms, a cheap pre-router, and a human-in-the-loop staff dashboard.
need_notes: Dispute friction is real but the pitch is generic and undocumented; no evidence or user insight in repo.
wow_moment: Type 'I don't recognize this charge', get a triage card that asks whether you made it, lock the card and open a claim, then flip to the staff dashboard, approve it, and watch the balance credit appear.
score_rationale: Solid Compound-track fit with an unusually careful agent safety design across three apps, all wired to Firestore. Held back by a generic chatbot premise, no README or evidence of need, no tests, and full dependence on paid Claude calls during the demo.
judge_summary: A bank chatbot that refuses to act: it classifies intent cheaply, reads only your own data, hands you a server-built dispute or fraud form, and routes the case to a staff dashboard that credits the account. Well-engineered, conventional to look at.

one_liner: Barcode-scan inventory tracker and cold-start demand predictor for small food businesses: a brand-new shop gets a day-one forecast borrowed from peer shops, blended toward its own data as history accrues, with reorder and expiry actions. No language model anywhere.
problem: Independent restaurants run out on busy game days and throw away expired stock; existing forecasting tools need months of sales history before they say anything useful.
target_user: Owners of small independent food businesses (pizzerias, taquerias, cafes), especially newly opened ones.
stack: better-sqlite3 (persisted to MongoDB Atlas or Postgres on Vercel)
core_loop: Phone camera scans EAN-13 -> /api/scan -> lots with expiry (FEFO) -> forecast.ts: EWMA level x weekday profile x event multiplier (Pitt/Steelers games, holidays, exams, own deals) for own history, median size-normalized peer prior, blended w = n/(n+14) -> reorder list with safety stock and case rounding, 'use it or donate it' list for lots expiring before demand consumes them -> dashboard widgets and /stats live counters; onboarding a new shop by name/type/seats/ZIP yields an immediate peer-based forecast; CSV import, checklist, events calendar, plain-English product lookup (rule-based).
mocked_or_hardcoded: All data synthetic (five peer shops, 12 weeks of demo usage, fake barcodes) generated by scripts/seed.ts; event multipliers are fixed estimates; donation partners are placeholders; catalog lookup hits Open Food Facts / Open Library live. Backtest (11-16% MAPE) is on synthetic peers generated by the same process, which the README states plainly.
demo_risks: Low: runs fully offline with SQLite; camera needs HTTPS or localhost (dev:https and tunnel instructions provided); Vercel copy persists to Mongo/Postgres. Seed must be re-run the morning of the demo so events line up (documented).
ui_experience: Custom design with a 'kitchen ticket' motif (torn paper slips on a rail for event days), Bricolage Grotesque headings, basil/tomato/cheese palette, customizable widget dashboard, forecast chart with a what-if 'days of history' slider and own-vs-peer source bar, phone scanner page, products table with natural-language filter chips, calendar view, CSV import preview. Roughly 20 routes. Attractive and interactive.
integrity_flags: First three commits ('Stockd Team', 16:22-16:40 EDT on 9/19) land ~7k lines in 15 minutes, and COMMIT_GUIDE.md instructs teammates to unzip 'stockd-features.zip' and commit 7 features in 9 commits, so most code was generated outside the repo (within the event window) and pushed in bulk. README demo-video/slides/Devpost placeholders unfilled.
ai_scaffolding_flags: No CLAUDE.md/AGENTS.md; COMMIT_GUIDE.md and DEPLOY docs read like agent output. Docs (~480 lines) are small next to ~10k lines of code and tests.
novelty_notes: Inventory management is a crowded category; the cold-start peer prior with an explicit blend weight, local event calendar and expiry-aware waste routing is a distinctive, well-explained mechanism.
need_notes: Specific user with a real two-sided loss (stockouts vs waste); argument is credible and the README is candid about synthetic evidence, but no operator interviews or real data.
wow_moment: Drag the 'what if it only had N days of history' slider from 84 to 0 and watch the forecast line swing from the shop's own data onto the peer prior; then scan a barcode off the laptop screen with a phone and see stock and stats move.
score_rationale: Nails No Wrapper (explicit no-LLM, explainable statistics, backtest, unit tests) and credibly stacks with Compound. Very complete, deployable, with a distinctive interactive chart and phone scanning. Novelty is moderate and all evidence is synthetic; bulk-pushed generated code is worth a look.
judge_summary: A no-LLM inventory forecaster for small restaurants that gives a new shop a day-one prediction from peer shops and blends toward its own scans over time. Polished, tested, phone-scannable, with a slider that shows the blend happening.

one_liner: A Chrome side-panel extension that sends a news article's paragraphs to a Nemotron pipeline, highlights propaganda techniques (SemEval taxonomy) in the page only when the quoted span exists verbatim, extracts checkable claims, and pulls related coverage from other outlets.
problem: Readers cannot see loaded language, straw men or unsupported claims while reading, and bias tools rate outlets rather than the specific sentences in front of you.
target_user: News readers who want an in-page audit of rhetorical techniques and claims; media-literacy use.
stack: Chrome MV3 extension (Vite + React + TypeScript, side panel, content script with closed shadow root)
Nemotron via NVIDIA API (nemotron-3-super-120b labeler, nano-30b classifier) with JSON schema response_format
core_loop: Side panel Analyze -> content script parses paragraphs and section hint -> background worker POSTs /analyze with Supabase token -> rate limit -> resolve doc type (metadata or small model) -> paragraphs batched by 5, labeled concurrently by Nemotron (flags + claims JSON) within a 60 s budget -> grounding gate keeps only quotes found verbatim in their paragraph -> doc type upgraded to slight/heavy bias by flag count -> response highlighted in the page with hover tooltips and listed in Summary/Claims tabs; Coverage tab -> /coverage -> ddgs news search on title+entities -> Nemotron writes a neutral summary of other outlets.
mocked_or_hardcoded: No mocks. Analysis caching is a TODO; failed batches are silently dropped (only logged). The eval harness (SemEval span F1, symmetry, grounding, routing) described at length in README/docs does not exist: eval/ contains an empty README and __init__.py.
demo_risks: Needs NVIDIA API key and latency headroom (multi-batch Nemotron calls on a long article), a Supabase project for sign-in, Postgres for rate limits, and DuckDuckGo search availability for coverage. Extension must be built and loaded unpacked. Real news sites' DOMs may parse poorly.
ui_experience: Side panel with sign-in, Analyze, Summary/Claims/Coverage tabs; in-page paragraph highlights with technique labels, hover tooltips and a pointer-following glow effect; 'design overhaul' commits late night. Interactive on any real article, which is a strong demo surface.
integrity_flags: auth-response.json committed at repo root with a live Supabase access_token, refresh_token and user record (credential leak). Repo skeleton and README pushed 09:44-10:11 EDT on 9/19, just before the 11:00 start; substantive code after. CLAUDE.MD and AGENTS.MD existed and were deleted at 16:24 on 9/19. README overstates the repo (describes routes, clients, tests and an eval harness that are not present).
ai_scaffolding_flags: docs/ holds ~1,600 lines of spec/plan (architecture.md, project-structure.md, build-checklist.md assigning tasks per person) written in agent-briefing style; deleted CLAUDE.MD/AGENTS.MD in history. Code (~5.4k lines) still exceeds docs.
novelty_notes: Span-level propaganda-technique detection inside the page with a hard grounding gate and cross-outlet coverage is a fresher take than outlet-level bias meters.
need_notes: Broad, plausible media-literacy need; no user evidence.
wow_moment: Open a real news article, press Analyze, and watch 'reckless scheme' and similar phrases light up in the page with technique labels, then flip to Coverage to see what other outlets said.
score_rationale: Strong Xtract fit (documents to traceable signals) and a clear non-chat Nemotron role, but the promised eval evidence is absent, weakening the Nemotron-track claim. Pipeline and extension are wired and demo-able on live sites. Committed auth tokens and an over-promising README are hygiene flags.
judge_summary: A Chrome extension that highlights propaganda techniques and claims inside the article you are reading, backed by a Nemotron pipeline that throws away any quote it cannot find verbatim. Good live demo; the evaluation it advertises was never built.
